literature_notes: All three ledger lines (L1, L2, L3) concern PCDH15 (Protocadherin-15), not CD2 (T-cell surface antigen CD2). The phrase 'CD2 domain' in those clips refers to a structural cadherin-like repeat domain within PCDH15 that is named after the CD2 protein fold — it is a domain OF PCDH15, not the CD2 protein itself. No ledger line reports a tag insertion in full-length, membrane-anchored CD2. Additionally, L3 explicitly states that FLAG immunoreactivity 'could not be detected' in the PCDH15-CD2 knock-in hair cells, meaning even the PCDH15 insertion was not successfully detected and would not qualify as a tolerated insertion under the ledger rules. Because no ledger line grounds a tag on CD2 (T-cell surface antigen, UniProt P06729) at any position — terminal or internal — zero sites are reported.
